questions.question: According to the Stanford classification, any aortic dissection involving the ASCENDING aorta is classified as:
questions.detail: Type A dissections involve the ascending aorta regardless of the entry site and typically require emergent surgical management.

questions.question: A "DeBakey Type II" dissection is defined as a dissection that:
choices: Is confined to the descending aorta
Is confined to the ascending aorta
Starts in the arch and extends distally
questions.detail: The DeBakey system focuses on the extent of the dissection: Type I (ascending + descending), Type II (ascending only), and Type III (descending only).

questions.question: On a non-contrast CT, the presence of a "hyperdense crescent" within the aortic wall is the hallmark of:
questions.detail: IMH represents hemorrhage into the media without a visible intimal flap; it is best seen as a high-attenuation crescent (60–70 HU) on unenhanced scans.

questions.question: In a patient with an aortic dissection, the "true lumen" is characteristically distinguished from the "false lumen" by being:
choices: Often smaller, with faster contrast opacification
questions.detail: The true lumen is usually smaller and opacifies earlier, while the false lumen is typically larger and may contain thrombus or "cobweb" strands.

questions.question: The "beak sign" (an acute angle between the dissection flap and the outer wall) is a reliable indicator of:
questions.detail: The beak sign is a characteristic feature of the false lumen in an aortic dissection.

questions.question: A "penetrating atherosclerotic ulcer" (PAU) is characterized on CT by:
choices: A focal, mushroom-shaped contrast outpouching through a calcified plaque
A hyperdense crescent on non-con images
questions.detail: PAUs occur when an atherosclerotic plaque ulcerates and penetrates the internal elastic lamina into the media.

questions.question: "Static" branch vessel obstruction in the setting of a dissection occurs when:
choices: The flap acts as a "shutter" during the cardiac cycle
The dissection entry extends directly into the branch vessel
The vessel arises from the true lumen only
questions.detail: Static obstruction involves the extension of the dissection into the vessel wall itself, whereas dynamic obstruction is due to the flap prolapsing over the vessel origin.

questions.question: Which of the following is an "indirect" sign of acute aortic rupture on CT?
questions.detail: While the flap is a direct sign of dissection, a surrounding hematoma is a critical indirect sign of containment failure or rupture.
